title: Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization with XGBoost for Alzheimer’s Disease Classification Using Multimodal ADNI Biomarkers
content: Background: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is one of the most pressing health challenges of our time, affecting roughly 55 million people worldwide and remaining the leading cause of dementia. Catching the disease early matters because timely care depends on being able to tell, with reasonable confidence, whether someone is cognitively normal (CN), shows mild cognitive impairment (MCI), or has already progressed to AD. Most existing machine learning approaches struggle here, largely because they chase a single performance metric and end up ignoring the trade-offs that actually matter in a clinical setting. To address this gap, we use the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) dataset and propose a Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization (MO-PSO) framework paired with Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) for multimodal AD classification. Methods: FreeSurfer-derived MRI brain volumes (30 features), CSF biomarkers (Aβ42, total tau, p-tau; Roche Elecsys), ADAS-Cog scores, MMSE, and other multimodal data were evaluated for 406 ADNI Phase 1 individuals (CN: 118, MCI: 199, AD: 89).APOE4 genotype, and demographics (37 features total). MO-PSO simultaneously optimized three competing objectives: maximizing cross-validated AUC, minimizing prediction instability across folds, and minimizing inference latency. The algorithm explored 12 particles over 15 iterations (180 hyperparameter evaluations), converging on n_estimators = 184, max_depth = 2, and learning_rate = 0.039. The MO-PSO XGBoost was benchmarked against five baseline classifiers using 5-fold stratified cross-validation, and a systematic ablation study assessed modality-wise contributions. Results: MO-PSO XGBoost achieved the highest AUC of 0.9464 (sensitivity = 0.892, specificity = 0.822, accuracy = 0.872, F1 = 0.908), significantly outperforming Random Forest (AUC = 0.9392, p < 0.001), XGBoost with default parameters (AUC = 0.9379, p < 0.001), Gradient Boosting (AUC = 0.9350, p < 0.001), and SVM with RBF kernel (AUC = 0.9346, p = 0.003). Ablation analysis identified cognitive scores (MMSE, ADAS-Cog) as the dominant predictive modality (ΔAUC = −0.068 upon removal), followed by demographics and APOE4 (ΔAUC = −0.013), CSF biomarkers (ΔAUC = −0.005), and MRI volumes (ΔAUC = −0.002). The top predictive feature was MMSCORE (gain = 0.120), followed by TOTAL13 (0.113) and TOTSCORE (0.089Conclusions: A Pareto frontier of clinically useful solutions is produced by MO-PSO's principled approach to hyperparameter optimization, which concurrently balances accuracy, stability, and efficiency. With an AUC of 0.9464, the system delivers state-of-the-art classification performance on ADNI, highlighting the importance of multi-objective metaheuristic optimization in clinical machine learning pipelines.
